newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel rises after rate decision.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel rises after rate decision.

text.p: The Israeli shekel's representative rate was fixed higher against the dollar and the basket of currencies on Tuesday after the Bank of Israel decided to leave unchanged its key lending rate for June, dealers said.
The central bank said on Monday that it was holding its key lending rate for June unchanged at an annualised 13.9 percent, the level at which it has been since the end of February.
"The shekel rose today as investors expected a moderate rate cut of 0.5 percentage point or less. The rate decision led to higher demand for the shekel," said a dealer at Bank Hapoalim.

He added that activity was relatively low and that the basket of foreign currencies was now traded at the lower edge of its trading band. "Despite the fact that the basket was traded at the bottom of the band, the Bank of Israel did not intervene in the market," he said.
The Bank of Israel has been intervening regularly in the market to support the currency basket which has been trading at the bottom end of its trading band for four months.
The central bank did not set a representative rate on Monday because of the U.S. Memorial Day.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3940 shekels against 3.3980 on Friday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6947 shekels against 3.7041 on Friday.
On the crosses, the shekel traded against the yen at 2.9169 shekels per 100 yen compared with 2.9335 on Friday, and against the mark at 1.9969 shekels compared with 2.0093 on Friday.
In the late afternoon, the dollar was trading at 3.3930 shekels.
